heuristics.name: shared-function-random-mapping
heuristics.statement: One fixed r=64 r-adding walk function in GT from P fresh starts matches uniform random sampling with the 63/64 distinct-partition merge factor for the birthday bound, and merged-suffix tail steps sample distinguished points at density 2^-32.
heuristics.support: Reproduced in proof.md: Poisson(1) indegrees for fixed distinct r=64 multipliers (Teske Lemma 3.1 adapted to c0-coefficient partitions, independent of 32-bit exponent size), Harris 1960 rho length, pooled multi-start birthday, 63/64 refinement for non-merging same-partition pairs, exponential tail hits. Multiplicative-notation toy experiments confirm merging and recovery end to end.

heuristics.name: hash-bucket-independence
heuristics.statement: The 128-bit slot hash assigns distinct table keys to independent uniform buckets.
heuristics.support: Standard heuristic for splitmix64-class non-cryptographic hashes; single re-salt fallback bounds the damage from any deviation (second failure is a 2^-257 union event).

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
Success relies on the supported multi-walk random-mapping heuristic.
Instruction budgets are conservative analytic upper bounds, not measured assembly.
The 2^98-entry table is an analytic device.
Best-known-attack analysis via the admissible GT reduction, not novel cryptanalysis.
